driver: The guardrail rate counts every outcome a candidate's exposures produce, while the log the screen is scored on records only the outcomes produced before each session closed; units under the incumbent and most candidates come back to an exposure still on screen after their session times out and act on it in a new session that the outcome record credits instead, and one candidate's units almost never do, so that candidate clears the guardrail on the log's count and fails it in one cell once the late outcomes are attributed back to the exposures that produced them, which is found only by joining each unit's later outcomes to the items its logged session showed under a rule that keeps a shown item off later exposures; a solver who nets the leader's brought-forward outcomes over the window and reads the guardrail off the log files that candidate, and the candidate fourth on the natural estimate is the largest that clears every condition.
driver_concrete: Buyers who leave the home screen open after a carousel session times out come back and order straight from a tile still on screen; the orders extract credits such an order to the new home session it was placed in, and the render log's ordered_tiles, which the orders credited to each session tie to exactly, counts only orders placed in the session. Under the incumbent and five policies these come-back orders run at 1.2 to 1.7 per 1,000 sessions, under the session-sequence model (C) almost never (3 in 16,544 sessions, none in app 0-29), so C, the largest lift over the test, clears the eight-cell guardrail on ordered_tiles (-1.0 per cent in app 0-29) and fails it (-3.8 per cent) once the carousel order rate counts every order placed from the tiles it served (charter 2.4), found by joining each buyer's carousel orders to the logged session's six tiles by listing (a shown listing stays off that buyer's carousel for seven days); a solver who nets the velocity boost's brought-forward watch-list orders but reads the guardrail off the logger files C, and E, the sequence ranker with the fresh-listing interleave, is the largest lift that clears every condition.
stump: A competent solver scores all six registered policies with the session-weighted estimator that alone reproduces the nine archived carousel tests, takes the charter's lift as the orders the arm's buyers place over the test (which nets the velocity boost's brought-forward watch-list orders), reads condition (b) in the eight platform-by-tenure cells on the render log's ordered_tiles and commits the Q1 2027 slot to C, the session-sequence model, at 9.8 extra orders per 1,000 carousel sessions; the step that lands it there is taking the logger's in-session tile orders as the charter's carousel order rate, when the charter counts every order placed from the tiles an arm served and buyers under every other ranker come back to order from a tile left on screen after the session closes (credited to the new session, so only the listing ties the order to its tile), which puts C's rate in app 0-29 3.8 per cent below the incumbent's, so C fails (b) and E, at 5.7, is the largest lift that clears every condition.
